title: Problem Overview: Splitting Sumsets with Positive Density
content: Erdos Problem #741 (Burr-Erdos 1994) asks two related questions about partition regularity of sumsets. Part 1: if A+A has positive upper density, can A always be split into A_1 and A_2 (disjoint union) with both A_1+A_1 and A_2+A_2 having positive density? Part 2: does there exist a basis of order 2 where no partition makes both sumsets syndetic? Erdos believed he could construct such a basis but 'could never quite finish the proof.' Both parts remain OPEN.
mathContext: Part 1: $\bar{d}(A+A) > 0 \Rightarrow \exists A = A_1 \sqcup A_2, \bar{d}(A_1+A_1) > 0 \wedge \bar{d}(A_2+A_2) > 0$? Part 2: $\exists A$ basis of order 2, $\forall A = A_1 \sqcup A_2, \neg(\text{IsSyndetic}(A_1+A_1) \wedge \text{IsSyndetic}(A_2+A_2))$? Here $\bar{d}(S) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} |S \cap [0,n]|/(n+1)$.

title: Upper Density and HasPosDensity
content: upperDensity A uses Filter.limsup to compute the limsup of |A intersection Iic(n)|/(n+1), where ncard counts elements of the finite set A intersect [0,n]. HasPosDensity A is the predicate 0 < upperDensity A. This is the standard notion of upper Banach density restricted to natural numbers.
mathContext: $\bar{d}(A) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{|A \cap [0,n]|}{n+1}$ via `atTop.limsup`. `HasPosDensity(A) := 0 < \bar{d}(A)$. Uses `Set.ncard` for cardinality of `A \cap \text{Set.Iic } n$`, cast to $\mathbb{R}$ and divided by $n+1$.

title: Sumset: Pairwise Sums
content: sumset A B = {n : exists a in A, exists b in B, n = a + b}, the set of all pairwise sums. This is the standard Minkowski sum restricted to natural numbers. The self-sumset A+A = sumset A A consists of all a + a' for a, a' in A (not necessarily distinct).
mathContext: $A + B = \{a + b : a \in A, b \in B\}$. Defined as `\{n \mid \exists a \in A, \exists b \in B, n = a + b\}$. Self-sumset $A + A$ includes both $2a$ (when $a = a'$) and $a + a'$ (when $a \neq a'$).

title: Basis of Order 2 and Syndetic Sets
content: IsBasisOrder2 A means every sufficiently large natural number is in A+A, formalized as Filter.Eventually (membership in sumset A A) atTop. This is weaker than A+A = N since finitely many exceptions are allowed. IsSyndetic S means bounded gaps: there exists g such that every interval [n, n+g] contains an element of S. Syndetic is strictly stronger than positive density: syndetic implies density >= 1/(g+1) > 0.
mathContext: `IsBasisOrder2(A) := \forall^\infty n, n \in A + A$` via `Filter.Eventually ... atTop`. `IsSyndetic(S) := \exists g, \forall n, \exists m \in S, n \leq m \leq n + g$. Syndetic $\Rightarrow$ $\bar{d}(S) \geq 1/(g+1) > 0$, but not conversely.

title: The Two Open Conjectures
content: ErdosProblem741_density formalizes Part 1: for all A with HasPosDensity(sumset A A), there exist A_1, A_2 with A = A_1 union A_2, Disjoint A_1 A_2, and both HasPosDensity(sumset A_1 A_1) and HasPosDensity(sumset A_2 A_2). ErdosProblem741_basis formalizes Part 2: there exists A with IsBasisOrder2 A such that for all disjoint partitions A = A_1 union A_2, not both IsSyndetic(sumset A_1 A_1) and IsSyndetic(sumset A_2 A_2). The two parts are in tension: Part 2 would provide a counterexample to the strongest version of Part 1.
mathContext: $\text{Part 1}: \forall A, \bar{d}(A+A) > 0 \Rightarrow \exists A = A_1 \sqcup A_2, \bar{d}(A_1+A_1) > 0 \wedge \bar{d}(A_2+A_2) > 0$. $\text{Part 2}: \exists A \text{ basis}, \forall A = A_1 \sqcup A_2, \neg(\text{Synd}(A_1+A_1) \wedge \text{Synd}(A_2+A_2))$.

title: Sumset Algebraic Properties (10 Proved Theorems)
content: Ten structural results about sumsets, all fully proved. sumset_comm: A+B = B+A (by swapping existential witnesses with omega). empty_sumset, sumset_empty_left/right: sumsets involving empty sets are empty (by simp). sumset_mono: A subset B implies A+A subset B+B. sumset_mono_left: monotonicity in the first argument. zero_mem_sumset_self: 0 in A implies 0 in A+A. double_mem_sumset: a in A implies 2a in A+A. sumset_union_contains_left/right: A+A and B+B are both subsets of (A union B)+(A union B).
mathContext: Key proved results: $A + B = B + A$ (`sumset_comm`), $A \subseteq B \Rightarrow A+A \subseteq B+B$ (`sumset_mono`), $a \in A \Rightarrow 2a \in A+A$ (`double_mem_sumset`), $A+A \subseteq (A \cup B)+(A \cup B)$ (`sumset_union_contains_left`). Proofs use `ext`, `rintro`, `omega`, and `Set.subset_union_left/right`.

title: Partition Properties (3 Proved Theorems)
content: Three results about disjoint partitions. trivial_partition: A = A union empty with Disjoint A empty (by simp and disjoint_bot_right). complement_partition: for any A_1 subset A, A = A_1 union (A \ A_1) with Disjoint A_1 (A \ A_1), proved by cases on membership and disjoint_sdiff_self_right. partition_membership: in a disjoint partition, x in A_1 implies x not in A_2, from Set.disjoint_left.
mathContext: `trivial_partition : A = A \cup \emptyset \wedge \text{Disjoint } A\ \emptyset$. `complement_partition : A_1 \subseteq A \Rightarrow A = A_1 \cup (A \setminus A_1) \wedge \text{Disjoint}$. `partition_membership : \text{Disjoint } A_1\ A_2 \Rightarrow x \in A_1 \Rightarrow x \notin A_2$.

title: Syndetic Set Theory (5 Proved Theorems)
content: Five structural results about syndetic sets. nat_syndetic: N is syndetic with gap 0. empty_not_syndetic: the empty set is not syndetic (any witness m would be in empty). syndetic_nonempty: syndetic sets are nonempty (take n=0 in the gap condition). syndetic_mono: supersets of syndetic sets are syndetic (transfer witnesses). syndetic_infinite: syndetic sets are infinite (for any n, the gap condition produces an element > n, proved via Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt).
mathContext: `nat_syndetic : IsSyndetic(\mathbb{N})` with $g = 0$. `empty_not_syndetic : \neg\text{IsSyndetic}(\emptyset)$. `syndetic_mono : S \subseteq T \Rightarrow \text{IsSyndetic}(S) \Rightarrow \text{IsSyndetic}(T)$. `syndetic_infinite : \text{IsSyndetic}(S) \Rightarrow S.\text{Infinite}$, using `Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt` and the gap condition at $n+1$.

title: Density Properties (5 Axioms)
content: Five axioms characterizing upper density behavior. density_empty: d(empty) = 0. density_finite: finite sets have density 0. density_mono: A subset B implies d(A) <= d(B). density_univ: d(N) = 1. density_le_one: d(A) <= 1 for all A. These are standard properties of upper Banach density that could in principle be proved from the limsup definition but are axiomatized to keep the formalization focused.
mathContext: Axioms: $\bar{d}(\emptyset) = 0$, $A$ finite $\Rightarrow \bar{d}(A) = 0$, $A \subseteq B \Rightarrow \bar{d}(A) \leq \bar{d}(B)$, $\bar{d}(\mathbb{N}) = 1$, $\bar{d}(A) \leq 1$. These characterize upper density as a finitely subadditive, monotone, normalized set function.

title: Basis Properties: Infiniteness and Positive Density
content: basis_infinite (PROVED): a basis of order 2 must be infinite. Proof by contradiction: if A is bounded by n, then A+A is bounded by 2n, contradicting the Eventually condition which requires arbitrarily large elements in A+A. Uses Filter.Eventually, Filter.mem_atTop_sets to extract the threshold N, then takes max(N, 2n+1) for the contradiction. cofinite_density_one (axiom): cofinite sets have density 1. basis_has_pos_density_sumset (PROVED): a basis has HasPosDensity(A+A), since A+A is cofinite (by definition of basis) and cofinite sets have density 1 > 0.
mathContext: `basis_infinite : IsBasisOrder2(A) \Rightarrow A.\text{Infinite}$. Proof: if $A \subseteq [0,n]$ then $A+A \subseteq [0,2n]$, but $\forall^\infty m, m \in A+A$ requires $\max(N, 2n+1) \in A+A$, contradiction. `basis_has_pos_density_sumset` uses `cofinite_density_one` and `norm_num` to show $1 > 0$.

title: Connections Between Parts: Tension Theorem
content: Two key theorems connecting the conjectures. part2_gives_non_syndetic (PROVED): if Part 2 holds, then for the constructed basis, every partition has at least one non-syndetic sumset (by push_neg and contradiction). syndetic_has_pos_density (axiom): syndetic implies positive density. part2_contradicts_part1_for_basis (PROVED): if Part 2 holds, then there exists a specific set A with HasPosDensity(A+A) where Part 1 fails for syndetic partitions. This formally establishes the tension between the two parts.
